versions.summary: Built the reference’s stocky ivory astronaut with a large dark visor, metallic helmet fittings, orange sleeve and knee panels, chest controls, gloves and heavy boots. One character in a symmetric palms-down T-pose, with connected joints, separated straight legs, grounded soles and humanoid joint coordinates. Inferred rear suit and backpack surfaces; reduced the backpack and shortened hoses, omitting the projecting antenna and external canister to keep anatomy accessible. Geometry is unrigged. Front, side, back and movement-test renders were unavailable; shoulder, hip and glove deformation still require validation after rigging.

review.summary: The neutral FRONT, SIDE and BACK views show a recognizable astronaut with the reference’s oversized helmet, black visor, ivory suit and orange accents. The symmetric T-pose has horizontal arms, separated straight legs, planted feet and visibly connected anatomy through the neck, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and ankles. No extra scene content is visible. The backpack and hoses are simplified and close-fitting. Movement tests fail: walking produces long orange spikes beside both upper arms and distorts the helmet trim; crouching severely stretches orange knee geometry. The arm-bend view has substantial forearm occlusion, limiting assessment of elbow continuity.
issues: Correct elbow-band geometry or skinning influences to eliminate the long orange spikes visible during walking; keep sleeve details attached to their local arm regions.
Correct knee-pad deformation so crouching does not stretch orange surfaces into triangular sheets across the bent legs.
Keep helmet, visor border and collar components locally coherent during movement; eliminate the warped trim visible in the walk test.
Repeat all movement tests after correction and provide an unobstructed arm-bend angle showing both elbows, forearms and wrists.

versions.summary: Preserved the oversized helmet, black visor, ivory suit, orange accents and compact backpack. Inspected supplied FRONT/SIDE/BACK: neutral T-pose, separated limbs, connected joints and no extra scenery. WALK/CROUCH fail from sleeve spikes, knee stretching and warped trim; ARM BEND obscures forearms. Rebuilt bands and shallow knee pads directly into dense limb surfaces, joined visor trim into the helmet surface, baked all mesh coordinates and adjusted the skull pivot. Removed loose hoses; hidden rear shell, neck and boot interiors are closed. One character object with joint hints, no skeleton or skinning. Revised movement remains unverified: rerun walk, crouch and arm bend with an unobstructed front three-quarter camera showing both elbows, forearms and wrists; inspect local weights if stretching persists.

review.summary: The astronaut remains recognizable through its oversized helmet, black visor, ivory suit, orange bands and chest controls. FRONT, SIDE and BACK show a symmetric T-pose, separated legs, horizontal arms, planted boots and no extra scene content. The compact backpack and removal of hoses, tanks and antenna simplify the reference appropriately. However, the helmet appears separated from the collar, and movement tests fail: WALK and CROUCH produce severe triangular sleeve stretching; CROUCH also distorts the backpack and chest hardware. ARM BEND does not clearly demonstrate preserved elbow volume and connected forearms.
issues: Repair sleeve deformation around shoulders and elbows: ensure all material regions move together without vertices remaining stretched toward the neutral arm positions. Recheck WALK, CROUCH and ARM BEND.
Close the visible helmet-to-collar gap with connected neck geometry that remains continuous during head and torso movement.
Keep the backpack and chest controls attached to the upper torso without bending into elongated strips or intersecting the arms during CROUCH.
Provide a clearer angled ARM BEND render showing both elbows, wrists and hands so joint continuity and forearm volume can be verified.

versions.summary: Preserved the oversized helmet, black visor, ivory suit, orange bands and controls in one symmetric T-pose character. Added continuous underlying sleeves with dense elbow rings, local mesh coordinates, and an extended neck overlapping the lowered helmet. Shortened the backpack and narrowed chest controls to keep them above the waist and clear of the arms. Hidden geometry includes sleeve surfaces beneath bands and overlapping neck, glove and boot connections. Joint landmarks are supplied; the character is not rigged. Images and movement tests were not inspected, so deformation repair remains unverified. Recheck FRONT/SIDE/BACK joint continuity and limb separation, WALK/CROUCH stretching, and a three-quarter ARM BEND view showing both elbows, wrists and hands. Any remaining stretching requires inspection of application-generated skin weights.

review.summary: The oversized helmet, dark visor, ivory suit and orange bands preserve the astronaut’s identity. FRONT, SIDE and BACK show a symmetric T-pose, separated legs, horizontal arms, connected-looking anatomy and no extra scene content. The backpack is reduced and loose hoses and antenna omitted. Movement validation fails: WALK stretches the shoulders and orange bands into angular fins, CROUCH exposes a floating backpack and jagged ankle transitions, and ARM BEND retains visible boot artifacts.
issues: Reshape the shoulder transition and keep sleeve bands attached during arm lowering; eliminate the tall, stretched shoulder fins visible in WALK.
Correct the backpack attachment so it follows the upper torso without floating above the back in CROUCH.
Repair the shin-to-boot overlap and deformation on both legs; remove the jagged ivory patches visible in BACK, WALK, CROUCH and ARM BEND.
Stabilize the collar geometry during movement; its rings buckle into a wavy strip in WALK. Rerender all movement tests after correction.
